verdicts.reasoning: The answer names Supply Management as purchasing and managing suppliers and their relationships, matching the reference, and this is verbatim supported by the PDF page 52 passage on foundational elements.

The answer frames the efficiency/responsiveness trade-off and gives both sides (fewer locations with longer transit if customers wait vs. more stocking points for speed), matching the reference; each claim traces to the page 53 design passage and the page 54 note that multi-location inventory causes extra cost and inefficiency.

It correctly explains pre-building stock because seasonal peak demand exceeds capacity, mirroring the reference and the chocolate-manufacturer example; the supplementary points on stockout avoidance and supply risk are also drawn from the page 54 passages.

The core answer—suppliers able to ship goods safely and securely within the required time frame—matches the reference and the logistics passage on PDF page 55; the added delivery reliability/speed point comes from the page 21 passage.

The answer identifies EDI and lists purchase orders, ASNs and shipment status among the exchanged documents, covering the reference, and the full list plus barcode/RFID data elements appear verbatim in the page 60 passages.
Correctly assigns responsibility for maintaining the agreed-upon stock level at the customer's location to the vendor, directly entailed by the VMI passage on page 62.

The answer conveys the reference's substance—exercises surface vulnerabilities, test response plans and build preparedness—with support from the stress-test, joint table-top and FEMA workshop/TTX passages, although it overlooked the closest FEMA page 21 TTX chunk and its After Action Report detail.

It states the reference point that upstream origins should be traced and that some countries shut factories for days or weeks for holidays, which is directly stated in the FEMA page 26 supply-source passage.

The answer covers all reference items (standard inventory supply, resupply intervals, storage facilities and their power needs, JIT restock) plus seasonal influx and backup power, all explicitly listed in the FEMA page 27 inventory passage.

The answer conveys that limited supplier diversity undermines resilience and heightens disruption vulnerability, matching the reference's gist though without spelling out the 'fewer alternatives' mechanism; support is adequate, with a mild conflation of 'limited number of supplier countries' into 'limited number of sources'.
